name: Supremo
summary: A 1983-84 Star Comics hero whose secret identity was the real film star Amitabh Bachchan. He fought crime with muscle, brains and gadgets, and had no superpowers.
origin: In 1983 Pammi Bakshi, editor of the film magazine Movie at India Book House, overheard children arguing over who got to play Superman, Batman or Amitabh Bachchan. She pitched the actor a comic of his own on the Goa set of Pukar, where co-star Randhir Kapoor's habit of announcing that 'Supremo has arrived' gave the hero his name. Gulzar advised on scripts and Pratap Mullick designed the look.
powers: Great physical strength and fighting skill
Island base stocked with a submarine and a helicopter
Welder-style goggles and a chakra pendant as signature gear
No flight and no superpowers by design

storyline.title: The Lost Idol
storyline.beat: The first issue opens on a film set, then sends the hero to recover an idol from 1660 that criminals are trying to steal by blowing up the sunken ship that holds it.

storyline.title: Hijack and Invasion
storyline.beat: Early stories include a plane full of children seized by hijackers and an alien plot that switches off Earth's gravity so villagers drift upward.

storyline.title: The Lost City
storyline.beat: A bottled message leads Supremo to Atlantis, where he faces a telekinetic ruler who wants to study him.

storyline.title: Trafficking and the vanishing floor
storyline.beat: He breaks a child-trafficking racket in one issue and, in another, frees nuclear scientists held by an international terror gang in an abandoned mine.

storyline.title: Supremo and the Bandit Queen
storyline.beat: Children are vanishing, and Supremo traces the dacoit Malan Devi to a hideout behind a waterfall. FilmCompanion calls the story the Dacoit Queen tale, and it finds her grieving her dead son.

storyline.title: The Imposter
storyline.beat: The world comes to believe Supremo has become a serial bank robber, forcing the real hero to solve the mystery and clear his name.

storyline.title: Series stops
storyline.beat: After about ten issues the line stopped when its driving editor, Pammi Bakshi, moved abroad after her marriage.

gossip.text: The name came from co-star Randhir Kapoor, who kept announcing 'Supremo has arrived' whenever Amitabh Bachchan reached the Pukar set.
Bachchan agreed to the comic on two conditions: no caricature of him, and free copies for schools and orphanages.
Costume designer Pratap Mullick had not seen Bachchan's films and drew more than six designs before the actor picked the pink one.
Nearly all issues began with a note from Bachchan asking children not to reveal that he was Supremo.
Many assume Supremo had superpowers like Superman.
gossip.truth: He could not fly; his edge was strength, brains and gadgets.

gossip.text: Collectors' prices for old copies now start close to Rs 1,000 each, against an original cover price of Rs 3.50, later Rs 4.

quiz.q: Who gave Supremo his name on a film set?
quiz.why: Randhir Kapoor used the word for Bachchan on the Pukar set and the editor adopted it.

quiz.q: Which real person was Supremo's secret identity?
quiz.why: The series was officially titled The Adventures of Amitabh Bachchan.

quiz.q: What did Supremo wear as his signature pendant?
quiz.why: His outfit paired a pink bodysuit with welder-style goggles and a chakra pendant.

quiz.q: Which animal was Supremo's intelligent scout?
quiz.why: Shaheen the falcon was inspired by the bird in the film Coolie.

theme.tagline: A star by day, a hero by night.

timeline.title: A name from the Pukar set
timeline.note: Pammi Bakshi pitches the idea to Bachchan in Goa and adopts the name Randhir Kapoor used for him.

timeline.title: Star Comics launches the series
timeline.note: The Adventures of Amitabh Bachchan opens with The Lost Idol, with Hindi editions titled Kisse Amitabh Ke.

timeline.title: Bandit Queen cover
timeline.note: Supremo and the Bandit Queen is the only cover to carry the hero's own name; the other issues are titled for Bachchan.

timeline.title: Series ends
timeline.note: The run stops after about ten issues when Pammi Bakshi leaves India.

timeline.title: Rediscovered as a collectible
timeline.note: ThePrint revisits the comic and notes that copies once priced at Rs 4 now sell as collectors' items on eBay.

facts.text: A real, living film star was the hero's secret identity, and the comic's official title was The Adventures of Amitabh Bachchan; the Hindi edition went by Kisse Amitabh Ke.
Editor Pammi Bakshi got the idea after overhearing kids quarrel over who played Superman or Batman; one child insisted on being Amitabh Bachchan.
Most issues open on a film set: Bachchan is shooting a movie when the falcon Shaheen arrives with news of a crime, and in true Bollywood style the police turn up on the last page.
Bachchan said yes on two conditions: the hero must never become a caricature, and free copies must go to schools and orphanages.
Poet-filmmaker Gulzar was the script consultant, and the hero was meant as a blend of Superman, the Phantom and Bachchan himself.
Supremo's pals included a dolphin named Sonali and the falcon Shaheen, so the hero's base felt like a mini adventure park.
Pratap Mullick, the Amar Chitra Katha artist who later drew Nagraj, designed the look. He had not seen Bachchan's films and produced over six sketches.
To hide his identity Supremo wears large welder-style glasses and a skin-tight costume with a wrap that a 1983 magazine compared to the cloths worn by fishermen on India's west coast.
Supremo is a peanut-munching, music-loving hero who carries a Walkman wherever he goes.
His sidekicks Vijay and Anthony are named after famous Bachchan screen roles, and Anthony wears a top hat like the Amar Akbar Anthony character.
Shaheen, Supremo's intelligent falcon scout, was inspired by the falcon Allah Rakha in the film Coolie.
Supremo kept a private island with a submarine, a Mustang-style car and a helicopter, in the manner of the Phantom's hideout.
The comics are packed with film in-jokes, even a mention of Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poem Sone Machari, written by the star's own father.
In The Lost City the hidden nation is so advanced that even kindergarten children study hydrodynamics.
In The Lost City, Supremo wrestles a python while the telekinetic king Amand plans to keep him prisoner and run experiments on him.
In the Invasion issue, visiting aliens dislike Earth's gravity and build a machine to switch it off, so villagers start floating away.
In The Disappearing Floor, Supremo drops through a trapdoor into a pit with closing spiked walls and escapes by karate-chopping a wooden door and using a plank to lift himself out.
The comics slipped in film jokes, such as a kidnapper mimicking the Sholay coin toss and a boy singing from Amar Akbar Anthony.
The Disappearing Floor's henchman Scorpio, with flashy sunglasses and slicked hair, looks like the comic Gogo of Andaaz Apna Apna but is written as cruel and frightening.
In the Invasion issue, Supremo lifts a baby out of a floating cradle, leaves the child on a treetop and then forgets all about it, a gag that lands as pure slapstick.
FactorDaily notes that Supremo appeared before Krrish, Shaktimaan and even Nagraj and Super Commando Dhruva, making him one of India's earliest comic superheroes.

kidSummary: Supremo is the hero identity of the real film star Amitabh Bachchan in a 1983 comic. He has no superpowers, just strength, brains, a falcon scout and an island base with a submarine and a helicopter, and he keeps it all secret.

story.title: A star on set
story.text: Most adventures begin with Amitabh Bachchan shooting a film. A falcon named Shaheen arrives with news of trouble.

story.title: Becoming Supremo
story.text: He slips away, puts on a pink costume with welder-style goggles and a chakra pendant, and heads off. He cannot fly, so he uses strength, brains and gadgets.

story.title: Wild adventures
story.text: Supremo recovers an idol from a sunken ship, finds the lost city of Atlantis, and stops aliens who switched off Earth's gravity.

story.title: Secret kept
story.text: Nearly every issue begins with a note asking young readers to keep his secret. After about ten issues the series stopped, but it is remembered as a rare comic with a real star as hero.
